newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore will act if economy deteriorates - Goh.
newsitem.headline: Singapore will act if economy deteriorates - Goh.

text.p: The government is watching Singapore's economic slowdown and would "act decisively" if the economy heads for slower growth next year, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said.
The Straits Times reported on Tuesday that Goh had told a political meeting on Sunday that the city state's current slowdown should "inject a dose of caution" in Singaporeans.
"Some countries progress. Others regress. Just make sure that we belong to the category of successful countries," he said.
He said Singapore would continue to tax companies and individuals lightly and establish conditions for its citizens to create wealth and accumulate assets.
"The Singapore economy is maturing. Our wages and rents are high. Our population is ageing. We cannot avoid completely the structural problems now faced by the industrial countries," Goh said.

"But we are anticipating them and have taken steps to ensure that we will not suffer their high unemployment rates through workers' training and retraining, and continuous upgrading of our manufacturing and service industries."
